- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk-off or panic-driven volatility.
- After a price spike (forecast > 72), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 5% of peak or adjust to mean of prior 5-day range.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 1.0 to -0.1), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid premature sell-off.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 73 and true outcome drops below 68, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days; if below 65, increase by 2–4% to avoid underestimating support.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.35–0.67 values (neutral/weak), model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 1–2% to reflect hidden momentum.
